title: Unbounded Holevo additivity gaps in finite dimensions
abstract: We establish unbounded two-use Holevo additivity gaps in finite dimensions. For each sufficiently large fixed integer $K$ and all sufficiently large $n$, we construct channels $T_n$ with output dimension $K^n$, input dimension $\exp(Θ_K(n^2))$, and \[   χ(T_n^{\otimes2})-2χ(T_n)   \ge n\left[\frac{\log_2K}{K}-2\log_2(1+9/K)\right]-O(1/n). \] The gap is linear in output qubits, with an explicit quadratic input-qubit cost and an explicit threshold on $n$. We also obtain channels whose single-use Holevo quantity tends to zero while their two-use Holevo information, and hence classical capacity, diverges. The channels arise from structured tensor products of the complementary mixed-unitary channels used in Collins's free-probabilistic proof. We establish minimum-output-entropy gaps by combining Collins--Youn's product-group Haagerup inequality with Bordenave--Collins's quantitative strong-convergence estimates
summary: This paper proves that quantum channels can exhibit unbounded two-use Holevo additivity gaps in finite dimensions. By constructing specific channels, the authors show that the classical capacity can diverge even when the single-use Holevo information vanishes. The proof relies on sophisticated tools from free probability and operator theory.
main_problem: The paper establishes the existence of unbounded two-use Holevo additivity gaps in finite-dimensional quantum channels, demonstrating a significant advantage in classical communication rate when using the channel twice versus using it twice independently.
main_result: It proves that for a sequence of channels, the single-use Holevo information can approach zero while the two-use Holevo information diverges, implying the channel capacity can diverge.
method: The proof combines advanced techniques from free probability (Haagerup inequality) with strong convergence estimates for tensor products of operators acting on finite-dimensional Hilbert spaces.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on quantum channels $\Phi: \mathcal{M}_d(\mathbb{C}) 	o \mathcal{M}_d(\mathbb{C})$, specifically constructed using structured tensor products of complementary mixed-unitary channels derived from free-probabilistic proofs.
key_observables: Two-use Holevo gap ($\chi(\Phi^{\otimes 2}) - 2\chi(\Phi)$), single-use Holevo quantity ($\chi(\Phi)$), and classical capacity ($C(\Phi)$).
important_parameters: The gap scales linearly with $n$ ($\Delta\chi(T_n) = \Theta_K(n)$), and the construction requires $n$ to be sufficiently large.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on combining Collins--Youn's product-group Haagerup inequality with Bordenave--Collins's quantitative strong-convergence estimates.
paper_structure: The paper builds the result by first establishing the gap using free probability tools, then relating this to minimum-output-entropy gaps, and finally proving the divergence of capacity by constructing a specific sequence of channels.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, constructive proof of superadditivity gaps in finite dimensions, which challenges classical assumptions about channel capacity and has implications for quantum communication complexity.
